recipes.name: Reuben Dip
ingredients_raw: 16 ounces sauerkraut, rinsed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix mayonnaise and dressing together in a small bowl; set aside.
Spread sauerkraut into a 9x13-inch baking dish. Layer corned beef, Swiss cheese, and mayonnaise mixture on top of sauerkraut.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Reuben Dip
raw_recipe.description: This baked Reuben dip made with corned beef, Swiss cheese, mayonnaise, and sauerkraut has all the flavors of a Reuben sandwich in a party appetizer.

video.description: Love Reuben sandwiches? Watch us take all the flavors of that sandwich and turn them into a dip. A layer of sauerkraut is topped with corned beef, Swiss cheese and a combination of mayonnaise and Thousand Island dressing. Bake it until heated and bubbly and enjoy with crackers, bread, or vegetables.

review.reviewBody:
I have used this recipe before and I put all the
ingredients together and then let cook in my crock pot for 4 hours. Then I serve it in my mini
crock pot in order to keep it warm.

Very good, to solve the cool and hardening problem that people commented on, I combined everything in a crock pot the day before serving and just kept it warm for the day of serving... worked great! I also added 5 sliced green onions and served this dip with rye chips and rye Triscuit crackers. Big hit for my game day party.

This is a total keeper and the crock pot is the way to go. I used 1/2 lb. corned beef shredded by the deli department at the grocery store. I also used dark rye bread chunks, but I think a rye cracker of some sort would have been better. Next time I make this, I will definitely try crackers or Triskets instead of rye bread. Very good recipe.

I'm making this for an appetizer for our Easter Brunch. It's cooking in my crock pot and I've taken a couple taster bites and it's AMAZING! I agree with all the other reviews! I bought 3/4 lb. Vienna Roast Beef from the deli and shred it up. I mixed that with 1 3/4 packages of shredded swiss. I rinsed the sauerkraut and dried it a bit by using my salad spinner. I mixed this with the other dry ingredients. In a separate small bowl I mixed 1 cup of Mayo (light) and 1 cup of dressing. Once I got a good mix on this, I then mixed it to the other bowl of ingredients. I mixed everything really well and put in my crock pot. I'm gonna warm it on low for a few hours and am looking forward to serving this to my family! It's delicious! Thanks for the recipe! Happy Easter!

Great! Just like a Reuben sandwich if you eat it with pieces of rye toast. Good with crackers too, but not quite Reuben without that rye. So for use with crackers or tostitos scoops, I recommend adding 1 tablespoon of caraway seeds, 1 tsp of dill, and a tsp of orange zest to Mayo/dressing mixture, which, together, provide a very rye-like flavor right in the dip.

This was delish!! I made this for a get together and now Everyone keeps asking me to make this. I also took the advice of others and used cream cheese. I double mine every time I make it so I will typically half the mayo & use a full block of cream cheese. We like these with rye bread & pumpernickel toasted bread squares. I buy a loaf of each, cut each slice into about 4 squares or whatever u feel is adequate for the size you want. I then place on a baking pan & toast in the oven about 4 min. Per side

I used this just to make regular rueben sandwiches just because its so much faster. I did use less mayo and more thousand island dressing and more than 8 oz of corn beef would be preferred. Just toasted my bread in the toaster and threw this mixture on the sandwiches. yum!! sure beat layering each individual sandwich and then toasting...

I made this for a big crowd for a Super Bowl party. I doubled the recipe....it went REAL QUICK! I served it with mini rye bread, mini pumpernickel, and wheat thins. I followed the recipe...BUT...I didn't use as much Swiss as it called for...it seemed to be too much. Also...I pushed down the corned beef and cheese layers with a fork, so it would get into the layer of sauerkraut, so there was a little of everthing in each bite. I also kind of pushed down some of the dressing layer into the other layers. It was gone in no time after it was baked...and I was asked for the recipe by several people. This is a keeper!!

Everyone at my party LOVED this! 
(including myself. Once everyone got a taste of it it was gone in no time!
I was short for time, so I mixed it all together & microwaved it for about 5 minutes & served it in my mini crockpot to keep it warm with a loaf of toasted rye bread cut into chunks for dipping. 
It was a HUGE hit! I will definitely make this one again.
This was so good! Made as directed except we toasted rye bread and just made sandwiches! So much easier to prepare and eat than a traditional reuben. My adult kids raved!

my family loved this. I used 6 oz. cream cheese, cubed, in place of the mayonaise. Also, as suggested didn't layer, but mixed altogether. Wonderful served w/ mini-pumpernickel loaf and rye flavored Truscuit
This recipe is awesome! Definitely needs more corned beef. But we mixed everything together and then spooned the mixture over party rye and baked them. Made rueben hanky panky!
Needs a bit more corned beef. Otherwise, incredible!
Great dip to serve at a party!
Add 1 t dill weed to the dressing combination!
Delicious and everyone loves it when I bring it
I make a Reuben Dip every year. This one is a keeper.

I accidently made this with Roast Beef and it did not have the zingggg. I added the Corned Beef and put it in the fridge and cut a serving the next day, zapped it in the microwave .... omygoodness !! soooo good !!

My wife and I are big fans of Ruben sandwiches . I made it for a Sunday football party and all my guests loved it . I was invited to a Super Bowl party and the hostess had asked me to make a double batch . The first two bowls of dip at the party to be empty !
